notes:
Account background: Scoutline is a mid-market SaaS company (product analytics) building an in-app assistant + semantic search for product managers and customer success. Started with Hosted API PoC in Oct 2025; demoed Dedicated in Dec. Customer wants move to Dedicated for cost predictability and data isolation.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-10-15: Intro call (AE Sofia) — requirement capture, latency targets, initial volume estimates.
- 2025-11-04: Hosted API PoC kickoff (FF call ff_2025-11-04_821b). Ran 2-week low-volume test with embeddings + reranking. Customer noted variability in token costs and wanted dedicated pricing.
- 2025-12-02: Dedicated demo (SE Liam) — walkthrough of Dedicated pool, autoscale, burst model. Liked KV caching and canary rollouts.
- 2026-01-10: POC (on-prem-ish VPC sim) — 3-day performance run: p95 latency chat ~160ms on model A, embeddings throughput = 1200 docs/s (avg 512d). Key obs: sustained throughput ok, warmup KV cache lowers token use.
- 2026-02-18: Pricing deep-dive (FF call ff_2026-02-18_3c9f) — discussed commit levels, burst allowances, overage bands, ramp schedule.

POC findings / technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: chat-driven help assistant (avg 800 tokens/session), embeddings for search + nightly rerank job.
- Targets: p95 generation <200ms (chat), embeddings latency <50ms, batch rerank throughput ~5000 queries/hour.
- Model preference: open models initially (Llama-derived / quantized), willing to test Redwood-verified variants.
- Routing/fallback: prefer hosted fallback during Dedicated maintenance windows.
- Data: must sit in VPC w/ customer-managed KMS; audit logs retained 12 months; EU residency for EU customers.

Pricing / packaging negotiation notes (detailed):
- Customer asked for 3 commitment scenarios (A/B/C) to compare. AE/SE prepared two drafts:
  * Scenario A (conservative): 4 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent), monthly commit $15k, 20% burst buffer (up to 5 GPUs) for short periods, overage billed per GPU-hour at $120/hr. 3-month ramp to full commit.
  * Scenario B (preferred by customer): 6 reserved GPUs, monthly commit $24k, 50% burst (up to 9 GPUs) with overage at discounted $95/hr after burst allowance, includes one free canary rollout per month. 6-month ramp schedule (month1 40% commit, month2 70%, month3 90%).
  * Scenario C (aggressive): 10 reserved GPUs, annual prepay discount (10% off), burst to 15 GPUs, strict SLA and dedicated support add-on.
- Overage mechanics: Redwood proposed tiered overage (0-10% at blended rate, 10-50% at higher rate) — Scoutline pushing for single flat overage to simplify forecast.
- Burst usage: customer wants predictable burst cap and a guaranteed price cap per GPU-hour. AE suggested soft cap with notification + guaranteed fallback to hosted at capped price if Dedicated saturated.
- Ramp schedule: customer insisted on gradual ramp to match revenue growth — asked for pro-rated ramp credits if actual usage lags commit by >2 months. Legal to approve.
- Credit / true-up: proposed monthly reconciliation with quarterly true-up; Scoutline requested monthly to match their rev ops cadence.

Stakeholders / internal champions:
- Product lead: Maya Brooks (technical champion, cares about latency + model parity) — quote: "Predictability > lowest price. We need budget certainty."
- CTO: Arjun Patel (security + residency gate) — running security review; asked for SOC2 evidence and KMS flow.
- Procurement: Jamie Ortiz — needs 2 internal approvals (finance + legal) before sign-off.

Open items / blockers (CRM style):
- Procurement approval for 12-month commit (procurement wants shorter pilot-first contract).
- Confirm EU residency option for EU customers (eu-west-1 pinned hosts).
- Finalize overage arithmetic (flat vs tiered) and burst pricing floor.
- Legal to review ramp/credit language (requested by customer).

Next steps (short bullets):
- AE Sofia to send revised commitment scenarios (A/B with number examples) by 2026-03-01.
- SE Liam to attach POC perf logs + recommended quantization profile (drive link).
- Commercial to propose a 3-month pilot contract (reduced commit) as compromise for procurement.
- Schedule procurement + legal sync (aim week of 2026-03-08).

Misc notes:

- Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations post-deploy (cache configs).
- Potential churn risk if overage rules remain opaque — flag as negotiation priority.
